docs.title: API Approach
docs.text: Any files in your deployScripts array that have a ".sas" extension will be sent to the relevant SAS Server for execution.

docs.title: Viya API deployment
docs.text:
The Viya deploy requires 3 things:

  • access_token
  • serverUrl
  • contextName

In order of priority, the access_token is taken from the.env.targetname file, then the .env file (if not found).

The serverUrl is the location of your Viya server. The contextName is the execution service on which your SAS code will execute. You can get a list of available contexts by running a GET to the following endpoint: /compute/contexts

docs.title: sasjs doc
docs.text: The sasjs doc command enables developers to generate HTML documentation directly from the comment headers used in SAS Jobs, Services, Tests, Macros and Includes. An example of the generated documentation can be found here. The comment headers must follow the Doxygen standard. It is possible to embed images, tables, bullet points, GIFs, links, and even raw HTML.

docs.title: Data Lineage
docs.text:
If the doxygen headers in any of the SAS Jobs or Services contain lists of data inputs and/or data outputs in the following format:

  <h4> Data Inputs </h4>
  @li libref.tablename1
  @li libref.tablename2

  <h4> Data Outputs </h4>
  @li libref.tablename3

Then a data lineage diagram will also be generated (linking data inputs to programs to data ouputs). In the diagram, programs will link to the documented program, and - if configured - the tables will link directly to the viewer in Data Controller.

Given that the same headers used to generate the documentation are used to compile the Services and Jobs, the documentation will naturally stay up to date - so long as you are using sasjs compile to prepare them.

Note

Jobs and Services are defined in the jobConfig.jobFolders and serviceConfig.serviceFolders arrays respectively. Lineage is NOT generated for macros (macroFolders) or programs (programFolders).

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Before using this command, you will need to install the SASjs CLI and Doxygen.

docs.title: sasjs doc
docs.text:
Generates HTML docs for all .sas files contained in the programFolders / macroFolders / jobFolders / serviceFolders listed in the sasjsconfig.json file, for all targets. If a specific target is provided, the generated docs will ignore content from the other targets.

sasjs docs is an alias for sasjs doc.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
sasjs doc -t <targetName> --outDirectory <sasFilePath>

sasFilePath - if this has a leading slash (eg /my-docs) then it must be the full path. If it is a relative path (without a leading slash, eg my-docs) then it will be pre-pended with the project root folder.

Additional arguments may include:

Option Alias Description --outDirectory -o Where to write the site. Defaults to sasjsbuild/docs (or the target's docConfig.outDirectory when it sets one). --target -t Generate docs from this target only, ignoring the other targets. The target can exist either in the local project configuration or in the global .sasjsrc file.

sasjs doc init takes no options - it writes the doxygen configuration into the project.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# generates docs in default folder i.e. ./sasjsbuild/docs, using all targets as a source
sasjs doc

# generates docs in default folder i.e. ./sasjsbuild/docs, using a specific target
sasjs doc -t viya

# generates docs in specific folder i.e. ./my-docs, using a particular target
sasjs doc -t viya --outDirectory my-docs

docs.title: sasjs doc init
docs.text:
For existing SASjs projects (eg those created prior to the implementation of the sasjs doc command, or where the doxy folder is otherwise uninitialised) OR to reset doxygen configuration/content, it is possible to initialise the config files using the sasjs doc init command.

This will create the 'doxy' folder under 'sasjs', and make it ready to use sasjs doc

For new projects using sasjs create, sasjs doc init is not required - the doxy folder and requisite files are created automatically.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: sasjs doc init

docs.title: Tips and Tricks
docs.text:
By default, the project title and description are taken from the package.json file in the root of the project. You can modify this behaviour (and many other doxygen defaults) by editing the sasjs/doxy/doxyFile file.

The docConfig options are also documented here

docs.title: ENV file
docs.text: Some values the CLI needs are environment variables rather than configuration: credentials, the access token, and a few switches that are useful when something misbehaves.

docs.title: Where the values come from
docs.text:
A .env file in the project root is loaded every time the CLI starts. When a command resolves a target, .env.<target> is loaded as well, so each target can carry its own credentials.

my-project/
├── .env           <- shared values
├── .env.viya      <- values for the `viya` target
└── .env.sas9      <- values for the `sas9` target

Both files are looked for in the current directory, and then in the directory above it. A variable that is already set in the shell wins over the file, so ACCESS_TOKEN=xxx sasjs deploy overrides whatever .env holds.

Neither file belongs in git. sasjs create and sasjs init add .env* to the project's .gitignore.

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
Variable Written by Read for ACCESS_TOKEN sasjs add cred, sasjs auth login authenticating against Viya and SASjs Server REFRESH_TOKEN sasjs add cred, sasjs auth login refreshing the access token when it expires CLIENT, SECRET sasjs add cred the client/secret used to obtain a Viya token SAS_USERNAME, SAS_PASSWORD sasjs add cred (SAS 9) SAS 9 authentication, and the username/password flow of sasjs auth login SASJS_CLIENT you the client id used when signing in to SASjs Server as a non-administrator LOG_LEVEL you how much the CLI logs - Info by default VERBOSE you request and response logging, see below macroCorePath you where to find @sasjs/core, overriding the usual search - see artefacts

sasjs auth login also reads SAS_USERNAME and SAS_PASSWORD so it can run without prompts in CI, and accepts --password-stdin for the password alone.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
VERBOSE=ON (case insensitive) logs a summary of every HTTP request and response, which is what to reach for when a server answers something unexpected. VERBOSE=BLEACHED does the same without the colour codes, for a log you will read later. Anything else, including VERBOSE=OFF, leaves it off.

Setting LOG_LEVEL=Trace in the same file has the same effect as VERBOSE=ON.

Note

Verbose mode can also be turned on for a single command with --verbose (-v) - for example sasjs job execute -v, or sasjs job execute -v bleached for the uncoloured version.

docs.title: What is the difference between local and global targets?
docs.text:
A target is a set of attributes (eg serverUrl, serverType, appLoc) to which a project will be deployed, or some code executed. When running locally, inside a project (eg a GIT repository) these attributes are taken from the sasjs/sasjsconfig.json file. By contrast, any (sensitive) authorisation attributes are retrieved from the .env.$(targetname) file, which is typically .gitignore'd for security.

When running outside of a project, the attributes are taken from the global ~/.sasjsrc file in the user home directory. In this case, authorisation details are also stored in the same file (authConfig).

The sasjs command will "discover" if it is inside a local project by the presence of a sasjs/sasjsconfig.json file in the current, or any of the parent directories. If not found, then the ~/.sasjsrc file will be searched instead.

It's worth noting that there are typically MORE attributes defind in a local target, because this is where an application is normally configured in detail for deployment. The global target is more for general use, such as running arbitrary jobs or SAS code.

A diagram of the rules for determining whether a local or remote target is used is available below.

docs.title: How can I obtain a Viya client and secret?
docs.text:
Tip

If you only need to run SAS code as yourself (e.g. sasjs run), you may not need a client/secret at all - try sasjs auth login first, which works with a regular SAS username and password.

For setting up the client / secret you will need the services of an administrator (a user with admin rights on the physical machine) as they need to query a protected file (the consul token). The client must be created with the 'authorization_code' grant type. If you are building a standalone application, it is also recommended to increase the expiry period of the refresh token to avoid manual re-authentications. The default expiry is 24 hours for an access token, and 30 days for a refresh token. This can be extended up to around 60 or 70 years.

docs.title: Viya 2025
docs.text:
The latest instructions are available here. Our recommended approach is to use the browser as follows:

  1. Open the following url as an administrator: https://<sas-server>/SASLogon/oauth/authorize?client_id=sas.cli&response_type=token
  2. This will redirect to a new url. Extract the access_token parameter and use it in the query below:
curl -k -X POST "https://viya-f0g8ht62vq.engage.sas.com/SASLogon/oauth/clients" \
   -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
   -H "Authorization: Bearer VERY_LONG_ACCESS_TOKEN_FROM_STEP_ABOVE" \
   -d '{"client_id": "YOUR_CLIENT","client_secret": "YOUR_SECRET",` \
      `"scope": ["openid"],"autoapprove":true,` \
      `"authorized_grant_types": ["authorization_code","refresh_token"],` \
      ` "redirect_uri": "urn:ietf:wg:oauth:2.0:oob"}'

This will create a YOUR_CLIENT and YOUR_SECRET client/secret pair using the authorization_code grant type (suitable for SASjs).

docs.title: Legacy Tools
docs.text:
SASjs provides two legacy tools for older versions of Viya:

Viya Token Web App

This is a web app for configuring a client & secret in multiple ways. Only valid for Viya 3.5

To deploy, see here: https://sasjs.io/apps/#viya-client-token-generator

Viya Token Macros

You can also generate a client / secret (and access / refresh token) using SAS code, on both Viya 3.5 and Viya 4, using the mv_registerclient macro.

/* compile the macros from github */
filename mc url "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sasjs/core/main/all.sas";
%inc mc;

/* create random client and secret on Viya 3.5 (admin rights needed) */
%mv_registerclient(outds=clientinfo)

/* create random client and secret on Viya 4 (consul token needed) */
%mv_registerclient(consul_token=12x34sa43v2345n234lasd)

This will generate a URL in the log, which must be followed to generate a refresh code (one time step). Paste that code into the macro below to generate an access / refresh token:

/* paste the code below */
%mv_tokenauth(inds=clientinfo,code=xET8ETs74z)

/* extract client, secret & token to the log */
data _null_;
  merge mv_tokenauth clientinfo(drop=error);
  put access_token=;
  put refresh_token=;
  put client_id=;
  put client_secret=;
run;

docs.title: How Does Authentication / Token Management work with SAS Viya?
docs.text:
For the client / secret flow (sasjs auth), the CLI will only work with pairs that have the 'authorization_code' grant type.

Alternatively, sasjs auth login authenticates with a SAS username and password (no client/secret required) using the password grant against the built-in sas.cli public client. See sasjs auth.

Once you provide the client (and secret) to SASjs, either as part of sasjs add or sasjs auth then a URL is presented to which the user must authenticate the CLIENT_ID.

Once the user provides the authorisation code, the CLI uses the client / secret / auth code to obtain an ACCESS_TOKEN and REFRESH_TOKEN.

The ACCESS_TOKEN may then be used for API requests until it expires. On expriy, or getting very close to it, the CLI will use the REFRESH_TOKEN to obtain a fresh ACCESS_TOKEN.

Once the REFRESH_TOKEN expires, the CLIENT must be re-authenticated using SAS Logon.

More information on token expiry is available here.

The below diagram illustrates this flow, but not precisely - the diagram describes the flow for a deployed application, where the secret can be secured at backend. In the SASjs CLI case the entire app is frontend (nothing to deploy at backend), and so the SECRET must also be kept on the frontend.

docs.title: Why does SASjs take so long to install?
docs.text:
Actually it doesn't, it should be fast. If you're waiting a long time (eg, over a minute) then the following may be the root cause:

  • Virus Scanner checking every file that is downloaded
  • Proxy settings (in which case, update the PAC file)
  • Slow network connection

The PAC file issue will only apply in corporate settings. The steps to address:

  1. Look in PAC for your proxy settings
  2. Set them in npm
    • npm config set proxy <<address>> -npm config set https-proxy <<address>>

docs.title: sasjs flow
docs.text:
The sasjs flow command allows SAS Administrators to configure a batch schedule using a JSON file, to trigger the batch using a command line, and to capture the results of the flow in a CSV file.

Jobs can be executed in parallel, or in sequence following the successful completion of the previous job(s).

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before using this command, you will need to:

  • install the SASjs CLI
  • add a deployment target.
  • Create a flow source (JSON) file.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
sasjs flow <action> [additional arguments]

Additional arguments may include:

Option Alias Description --source -s Path to the flow definition - a JSON file listing the jobs. Required. --logFolder -l Folder in which the job logs are saved. --csvFile -c Path of the CSV that receives each job's status. It is replaced if the command runs again. --streamLog Write each job's log to --logFolder while it runs, rather than at the end. Useful for a long flow. --target -t The target to run the flow against. Defaults to defaultTarget in sasjsconfig.json, then the global .sasjsrc.

docs.title: Source JSON file
docs.text:
This is the file where the pattern of the flow is configured. A very simple flow definition might look like this:

{
  "name": "simpleFlow",
  "flows": {
    "flow01": {
      "jobs": [
        {
          "location": "/Projects/subfolder/someJob1"
        },{
          "location": "/Projects/subfolder/someJob2"
        }
      ],
      "predecessors": []
    }
  }
}

The above is named "simpleFlow" with one flow named "flow01" and two Viya Jobs - which will execute in parallel (as they are in the same flow).

A more complicated one would look like this:

{
  "name": "myAmazingFlow",
  "flows": {
    "ourveryfirstflow": {
      "jobs": [
        {
          "location": "/Projects/job1"
        },
        {
          "location": "/Projects/job2"
        },
        {
          "location": "/Projects/job3"
        }
      ],
      "predecessors": []
    },
    "secondflow": {
      "jobs": [
        {
          "location": "/Projects/job11"
        }
      ],
      "predecessors": [
        "firstflow"
      ]
    },
    "anotherflow": {
      "jobs": [
        {
          "location": "/Public/job15"
        }
      ],
      "predecessors": [
        "ourveryfirstflow",
        "secondflow"
      ]
    }
  },
    "yetanotherflow": {
      "jobs": [
        {
          "location": "/Public/job115"
        }
      ],
      "predecessors": []
    }
  }
}

The above contains a flow definition with 4 flows:

  1. "ourveryfirstflow" - triggers 3 jobs at once, runs immediately as no predecessors
  2. "yetanotherflow" - triggers 1 job, runs immediately as no predecesors
  3. "secondflow" - triggers as soon as firstflow is complete and ONLY if the jobs all finish with SUCCESS status
  4. "anotherflow" - triggers once firstflow and secondflow are complete, but ONLY if all finish with SUCCESS

docs.title: sasjs flow execute
docs.text: Used to trigger the execution a flow of jobs on the SAS server.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
sasjs flow execute --source /local/flow.json --logFolder /local/log/folder --csvFile /local/some.csv -t targetName

The following arguments are optional:

  • logFolder - will default to the sasjsresults folder
  • csvFile - will also default to the sasjsresults folder
  • t - will default to the defaultTarget attribute (if available)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
# run the flow of jobs using the target defined in sasjs add
sasjs flow execute -s /local/flow.json -l /local/log/folder --csvFile /local/some.csv -t myTarget

This will schedule SAS jobs and execute them according to the flow definition in the JSON file. Job logs will be returned as ".log' text files and saved to the local (--logFolder) folder. Details of the Job Executions and their status will be saved to the CSV file.

docs.title: See Also
docs.text: • sasjs job execute

docs.title: sasjs folder
docs.text:
The sasjs folder command allows users to manage logical SAS Viya Folders (the kind that appear in SAS Drive). These are not to be confused with physical (filesystem) directories. The Viya Folder tree is actually stored in a Postgres Database.

It is useful to be able to create and delete folders as part of CI/CD, for instance when tearing down part of an environment in order to rebuild it.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Before using this command, you will need to install the SASJS CLI and add a deployment target.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
sasjs folder <action> [additional arguments]

Additional arguments include:

Option Alias Sub commands Description --target -t all The target whose server holds the folders. SAS Viya only. Defaults to defaultTarget in sasjsconfig.json, then the global .sasjsrc. --force create Delete and re-create the folder when it already exists.

Note

sasjs folder works on SAS Viya targets only - it manages SAS Drive folders, which SAS 9 does not have.

docs.title: sasjs folder list
docs.text: Used to list first level children folders of given folder.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: sasjs folder list <folderpath> -t target

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: sasjs folder list /Public -t myTarget

docs.title: sasjs folder create
docs.text: Used to create a new SAS folder. Will fail if the folder already exists. If the -f flag is used, a new folder will be forcibly created (ie, if there is an existing one, it will be deleted).

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: sasjs folder create <folderpath> -t target -f

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: sasjs folder create /Public/new/folder -t myTarget

docs.title: sasjs folder delete
docs.text: Used to delete an existing SAS Folder. To avoid the overhead with recursively deleting folders and content, the delete command actually moves the requisite folder into the Recycle Bin. This makes it very fast, as well as reversable.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: sasjs folder delete <folderpath> -t target

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: sasjs folder delete /Public/new/folder -t myTarget

docs.title: sasjs folder move
docs.text: Moves an existing folder to a new location. It behaves similarly to the Unix mv command. If targetpath is an existing folder, the folder will be moved underneath targetpath. If targetpath does not exist, the folder is moved and renamed, inside the parent folder. See examples below.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: sasjs folder move <folderpath> <targetpath>

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Moving folder to /Public

sasjs folder move /Public/old/folder /Public -t myTarget

Moving folder to folder2 leaving it in same directory

sasjs folder move /Public/old/folder /Public/old/folder2 -t myTarget

Moving folder to /Public and renaming to folder2 Reason for rename - /Public/folder2 does not exist.

sasjs folder move /Public/old/folder /Public/folder2 -t myTarget

docs.title: sasjs fs
docs.text:
The sasjs fs command allows users to manage a remote SAS (physical) filesystem from a local machine. No SSH or FTP accounts are necessary - the tool makes use of the APIs (Viya, SASjs Server) or a SAS EBI STP runner.

Not to be confused with:

  • the logical SAS Folders (eg SAS Drive or Metadata BIP Tree), managed using the sasjs folder command.
  • the regular sasjs compile command, which creates self-contained Jobs / Services / Tests that do not require a filesystem.

It is also possible to use this feature natively within the SASjs VSCode Extension - https://github.com/sasjs/vscode-extension#directory-synchronisation.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before using this command, you will need to:

  • install the SASjs CLI
  • add a deployment target (for all operations except sasjs fs compile)

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
sasjs fs <action> [additional arguments]

Additional arguments may include:

Option Alias Sub commands Description --target -t all three The target whose server holds the files. Needs serverUrl and serverType. Defaults to defaultTarget in sasjsconfig.json, then the global .sasjsrc. --local -l sync, deploy The local folder to send. A relative path is taken from the project root. --remote -r sync, deploy The folder on the SAS server that receives it. --output -o all three compile: the path of the program to write (a .sas extension is added). sync and deploy: a folder for the log. Both default to a timestamped folder under sasjsbuild / sasjsresults.

docs.title: sasjs fs compile
docs.text:
Used to generate a single SAS program that contains all the files (and subdirectories) of a given LOCAL folder. This program can be executed in any flavour of SAS to generate the files on the SAS server - simply set %let fsTarget=/your/target/folder; and run the program.

To preserve encoding and special characters, as well as to enable the compilation of binary content, all files are base64 encoded.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: sasjs fs compile <localFolder> -o <programPath>

docs.title: Usage

sasjs fs compile C:\my\project -o C:\temp\deployme.sas

  do while(fread(filein)=0);
    length raw $4 ;
    do i=1 to 4;
      rc=fget(filein,char,1);
      substr(raw,i,1)=char;
    end;
    rc = fput(fileout, input(raw,$base64X4.));
    rc =fwrite(fileout);
  end;
  rc = fclose(filein);
  rc = fclose(fileout);
run;

filename _in64 clear;
filename _out64 clear;

docs.title: sasjs fs deploy
docs.text: Compiles a local folder into a SAS program and executes it on the target in one step, so the files arrive in the remote folder without you saving and running the program yourself.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
sasjs fs deploy --local <localFolder> --remote <remoteFolder> [options]

The folders are passed with --local (-l) and --remote (-r); --output (-o) sets a folder for the log.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: sasjs fs deploy -l ./data -r /sasdata/mydata -t viya

docs.title: Deploy or sync?
docs.text: deploy always writes the whole tree. sync compares hashes first and sends only what differs, which is what you want for routine updates; deploy is for a first load, or when the remote copy is suspect.

docs.title: sasjs fs sync
docs.text:
Will hash up a remote SAS filesystem, compare with local hashes, and deploy only the differences. Will also create the folder(s) on the remote server if necessary (if the SAS user account has the requisite permissions).

Here's a demo video:

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
sasjs fs sync -l <localFolder> -r <remoteFolder> -t targetName

Can also be used without the arguments, taking values from the sasjsconfig.json file, eg:

sasjs fs sync

or

sasjs fs sync -t myTarget

docs.title: Known Limitations
docs.text:
The following issues exist with the current implementation - they do not affect the functionality (syncing local directory with remote) but we do plan to address them in a future release:

  • If remoteFolder path is relative, or contains a tilde (eg ./somedir or ~/somedir), the terminal response will incorrectly state that there were sync issues. This is due to path expansion affecting the comparison. In fact the files were deployed successfully.
  • If a file is deleted locally, it will not be deleted remotely. This part has not been built yet.
  • If a file in a subdirectory is renamed it will not be re-synced. This is due to hash compares at folder level being based only on file content. We will change the algorithm to include filenames when hashing folder content into a folder hash.

docs.title: sasjs help
docs.text: sasjs help prints the commands available in the installed version of the CLI, with a summary of what each one does.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
sasjs help

sasjs h is the alias.

The text is built into the CLI, so it describes the version you are running rather than the newest one on this site. When a command in the list does not behave as you expect, check sasjs version first - an older CLI is the usual reason.

Every command also has a page here: see the command table.

docs.title: Help for a single command
docs.text:
Each command accepts --help, which prints its syntax, options and examples:

sasjs job --help
sasjs compile --help

A command name that the CLI does not recognise answers:

ERROR  Invalid SASjs command! Run sasjs help for a full list of available commands.

docs.title: sasjs init
docs.text:
The sasjs init command turns a folder that already contains code into a SASjs project. Change into that folder and run:

sasjs init

It takes no arguments and works on the current working directory. Use sasjs create when you want a new project scaffolded from a template; use sasjs init when the SAS programs, jobs or other files are already in place and you want the SASjs tooling to work over them.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The SASjs CLI installed (sasjs init works without a deployment target - it does not contact a SAS server)
  • Network access, for the @sasjs/core install

docs.title: What it creates
docs.text:
Path Purpose sasjs/sasjsconfig.json Project configuration, including a placeholder target sasjs/macros/ The macro folder macroFolders points at - created with a .gitkeep so an empty folder survives a commit sasjs/doxy/ Doxygen templates used by sasjs doc .sasjslint Lint rules used by sasjs lint - created only if absent .gitignore Adds node_modules, sasjsbuild, sasjsresults and .env* if those rules are missing; existing content is kept package.json Created with npm init --yes if the folder has none, then @sasjs/core is added as a dependency

node_modules and package-lock.json follow from that install.

It does not create sasjs/services, sasjs/jobs or the rest of the layout, and it does not add a README - sasjs create is the command that lays out a full project.

docs.title: The generated sasjsconfig.json
docs.text:
{
  "$schema": "https://cli.sasjs.io/sasjsconfig-schema.json",
  "macroFolders": ["sasjs/macros"],
  "defaultTarget": "mytarget",
  "targets": [
    {
      "name": "mytarget",
      "serverType": "SASJS",
      "serverUrl": "",
      "appLoc": "/Public/apps/myapp"
    }
  ]
}

The single target is a placeholder. serverUrl is empty rather than a sample URL, because an empty value reads as "not configured yet" while a non-empty placeholder has to pass URL validation every time the configuration is read. Put the real serverUrl and appLoc in it, or add a target with sasjs add / by editing the file - see the configuration reference.

docs.title: Running it in a folder that is already a SASjs project
docs.text:
If the folder already contains sasjs/sasjsconfig.json, sasjs init aborts without touching anything:

$ sasjs init
ERROR  This folder is already a SASjs project (sasjs/sasjsconfig.json exists). Aborting without making changes.
$ echo $?
4

Exit code 4 is the only code that means the folder is already a SASjs project, so a script can branch on it. Code 1 covers an invalid command or invalid arguments, and code 2 a genuine failure.

The check looks at the current folder only. Initialising inside a folder that belongs to a project higher up starts a new project in that folder, which is what a repository holding several separate SASjs apps needs.

The refusal is deliberate. A target carries user data - serverUrl, appLoc, authInfo, contextName - and an unconditional write would replace it with the placeholder above. sasjs create writes a sasjsconfig.json of its own, so sasjs init is not needed after sasjs create, and running it there aborts too.

To re-run the initialisation, delete or move sasjs/sasjsconfig.json first.

docs.title: After initialisation
docs.text:
A freshly initialised project compiles straight away: the macro folder exists and the empty serverUrl passes validation, so no edit is needed before the first build step. Running sasjs compile in the folder compiles the project for the mytarget target.

Commands that talk to a SAS server - sasjs deploy, sasjs run, sasjs request and the authentication commands - need a real serverUrl first.

The other local commands work in the folder as they are:

sasjs build
sasjs doc
sasjs lint

The configuration, the build and deploy settings, and the target attributes are described in the sasjsconfig reference, and the full command list is on the home page.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: The SASjs CLI is available on Node Package Manager. To make NPM available to your terminal, it is first necessary to install NodeJS. The NodeJS installation will vary depending on your OS, as detailed below.

docs.title: Windows
docs.text:
If you only care about using the SASjs CLI then simply download NodeJS directly from the homepage: https://nodejs.org/en. We recommend you do NOT install chocolatey (leave the checkbox unchecked), unless you have a specific need for it.

If you're a power user looking to play with different versions of NodeJS and you have admin rights on your machine, then NVM-Windows would be the better choice - available here: https://github.com/coreybutler/nvm-windows#installation--upgrades

docs.title: Mac / Linux
docs.text:
We recommend using NVM instead of Node directly, as this does not require root permissions.

curl -o- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh/nvm/master/install.sh | bash
source ~/.bashrc
nvm install --lts

docs.title: 2. SASjs CLI
docs.text:
The CLI can now be installed using Node Package Manager (npm) as follows:

npm i -g @sasjs/cli

docs.title: Upgrades
docs.text:
Simply run npm i -g @sasjs/cli@latest to get the latest package.

Note - this approach is not reliable if you are using NPM v6. We recommend that you use the latest version of NPM, for security reasons. To update NPM, run: npm i -g npm@latest

docs.title: sasjs job
docs.text: sasjs job execute runs a job that already exists on the SAS server - a Viya job, a SAS 9 job, or a job on SASjs Server - and brings back what it produced.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• the SASjs CLI installed
  • a target, with credentials (sasjs auth)
  • the job already deployed, by sasjs deploy or otherwise

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
sasjs job execute <jobPath> [options]

exec is accepted in place of execute.

jobPath is the location of the job on the server. A path that begins with / is used as it is; a relative path is prefixed with the target's appLoc.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Option Alias Server types Description --target -t all The target to execute against. Defaults to defaultTarget in sasjsconfig.json. --log -l all Path to save the job log to. On Viya, supplying it also makes the CLI wait for the job. --output -o all Path to save the job's output to. --source -s all Path to a JSON file of job variables - {"macroVars": {"var": "value"}}. --wait -w Viya Wait for the job to finish before returning. --statusFile Viya Save the job status to this file as it progresses. With no path, the status is printed instead. --streamLog Viya Write the log to the --log path while the job runs, rather than at the end. Useful for long jobs. --ignoreWarnings -i Viya Return success when the job finishes in the warning state, rather than a failure. --returnStatusOnly -r Viya Deprecated - prints a warning and is ignored. --verbose -v all Log a summary of every HTTP request and response. -v bleached drops the colour.

SAS 9 and SASjs Server execute the job in a single request, so they have nothing to wait for and no status to poll: --wait, --statusFile, --streamLog and --ignoreWarnings are Viya only.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# run a job, keeping the log and the output
sasjs job execute /Public/folder/someJob -l ./jobLog.log -o ./jobOutput.json -t myTarget

# pass macro variables into the job
echo '{"macroVars":{"myMacVar":"my macro value!","macvar2":"another value"}}' > sourcevars.json
sasjs job execute /Public/folder/someJob -l ./jobLog.log -s ./sourcevars.json

# follow a long running job: wait, streaming the log, with status written out
sasjs job execute /Public/folder/someJob -w --streamLog -l ./jobLog.log --statusFile ./jobStatus.json

docs.title: What comes back
docs.text:
The log and the output are written where --log and --output point; with neither, nothing is fetched from the server.

The command exits with a non-zero code when the job fails, so it can gate a pipeline step:

sasjs job execute /Public/folder/someJob -w -l ./jobLog.log || echo "job failed"

docs.title: sasjs lint
docs.text:
The sasjs lint command is used to identify issues such as embedded passwords, trailing spaces, sloppy indentation, missing program headers and more, in your SAS code.

This means developers can spend less time on code reviews and formatting fixes, as well as preventing dangerous code, or code with hard-to-detect bugs from hitting production servers.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Before using this command, you simply need to install the SASjs CLI. It is NOT necessary to configure a sasjs/sasjsconfig.json file - the sasjs lint command can be executed from anywhere - including from within a git hook.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The lint settings are described here. The settings can be made in a project directory (/your/project/.sasjslint), with a fallback settings file in the home directory (~/.sasjslint). If a setting is not defined in either the project or the home directory, then the default value is used.

Linting is applied to all .sas files in all subfolders within the Project Directory. The rule for determining the Project Directory is as follows:

  • If the current directory contains a .sasjslint file, then use the current directory
  • Else search all parent directories for a .sasjslint file (ignoring the home directory) and if found, use that
  • If no .sasjslint file is contained in any parent directories, then use the current directory

For clarity, the Project Directory is printed to the console whenever running sasjs lint.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
sasjs lint [find | fix | init] [filterStrings..]
Action What it does find Reports violations. This is what runs when no action is given. fix Applies the fixes the configured rules provide. init Writes a .sasjslint configuration file for the project.

Each filterStrings narrows the run: a folder, an absolute file path, or a fragment of a file name. With none, every .sas file in the project is linted.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
The command works as follows:

sasjs lint

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: Simply run the command and the list of exceptions (along with line / column numbers) is shown in the console, eg:

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
The command works as follows:

sasjs lint fix

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Simply run the command and the exceptions are fixed! The following rules are supported for 'autofix':

  • noTrailingSpaces
  • hasDoxygenHeader
  • hasMacroNameInMend
  • lowerCaseFileNames

docs.title: Usage in a GIT hook
docs.text:
The sasjs lint command will return a non-zero exit code if any exceptions are found. A great way to prevent questionable code from ever hitting your GIT repo (let alone the production server) is to run the linter as part of a pre-commit hook.

To configure this, there are two steps. First, add the following to the "scripts" section of your package.json file: "prepare": "git rev-parse --git-dir && git config core.hooksPath ./.git-hooks || true"

Then, add the following to your .git-hooks/pre-commit file (see example):

#!/bin/bash

# Ensure lint is passing
LINT=`sasjs lint`
if [[ "$LINT" != "✔ All matched files use @sasjs/lint code style!" ]]; then
  echo "$LINT"
  echo "To commit in spite of these warnings, use the -n parameter."
  exit 1
fi

If you run sasjs create SOMEPROJECT -t jobs you can check out a sample project with this hook already configured. Or, you can just clone this repo and run npm prepare.

docs.title: Further Resources:
docs.text:
• Using the linter on terminal
  • Longer intro to sasjs lint
  • Source repo: https://github.com/sasjs/lint
  • SAS blog post: https://blogs.sas.com/content/subconsciousmusings/2025/05/30/automatic-linting-of-sas-code-with-sasjs/

docs.title: Sponsorship & Contributions
docs.text:
SASjs is an open source framework! Contributions are welcomed. If you would like to see a feature, because it would be useful in your project, but you don't have the requisite (TypeScript) experience - then how about you engage us to build it for you?

Contact Allan Bowe for details.

docs.title: sasjs request
docs.text: The sasjs request command enables developers to call SASjs web services from the commandline.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Before using this command, you will need to install the SASJS CLI and add a deployment target.

docs.title: sasjs request
docs.text: This will create a session and execute the relevant SAS service. The output will be returned as a file in the current directory (output.json).

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
sasjs request <sasProgramPath> [additional arguments]

sasProgramPath - if this has a leading slash (eg /Public/app/folder/servicename) then it must be the full path. If it is a relative path (eg path/servicename) then it will be pre-pended with the appLoc - defined in the config JSON file.

Additional arguments may include:

Option Alias Description --target -t The target to send the request to. Defaults to defaultTarget in sasjsconfig.json, then the global .sasjsrc. --data -d A JSON file of input data - the tables the service reads. --config -c A JSON file of configuration for the request. --log -l Where to save the log. Inside a project it defaults to sasjsresults, otherwise the current directory. --output -o Where to save the output. Inside a project it defaults to sasjsresults, otherwise the current directory.

docs.title: data structure
docs.text:
The input data is structured as follows:

{
    "tablewith2cols1row": [{
        "col1": "val1",
        "col2": 42
    }],
    "tablewith1col2rows": [{
        "col": "row1"
    }, {
        "col": "row2"
    }]
}

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# run a SAS Service without inputs, using the default target
sasjs request /Public/app/myApp/common/appinit

# run a SASjs web service with inputs and a config file
sasjs request common/getdata -d ./dataFile.json -c ./configFile.json -t myTarget

# run a SASjs web service with log and output files defined
sasjs request /Public/app/myApp/common/appinit -l ./jobLog.log -o ./jobOutput.json

docs.title: sasjs run
docs.text:
The sasjs run command enables developers to submit SAS code for execution from the commandline.

The log will be returned as a file in the current directory. The source file must have a ".sas" extension.

Note - an additional variable macro variable will be added by the adapter, with the value of the target appLoc and the filename (equivalent to %let _program=/My/AppLoc/runfilename.sas;). This is actually added as a session variable, so will not be visible in the logs.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Before using this command, you will need to install the SASJS CLI and add a deployment target.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
sasjs run <sourcecode> [additional arguments]

<sourcecode> can be a local file path or a URL.

Additional arguments may include:

  • --log (alias -l) - The full or relative (to the folder in which the command is invoked) path to the log file being created. If ommitted, the log will be created in the current directory, with a timestamp.

  • --source (alias -s) - Path to a JSON file that can be used to inject macro variables into the session. Useful for running existing programs in a "job like" fashion. The JSON file should have the following structure: {"macroVars": {"varname": "value", "var2": "val2"}}. This will result in the following code being injected into the session:

%let varname=value;
%let var2=val2;

  • --target (alias -t) - the target environment in which to deploy the services. If not specified, default target will be used, mentioned in sasjsconfig.json. The target can exist either in the local project configuration or in the global .sasjsrc file.

  • --compile (alias -c) - optional argument that is used to compile the program prior to execution. Useful for including dependent macros and includes. More info here.

docs.title: Using Github Urls
docs.text:
If using a URL from github, be sure to link to the raw version of the file, eg: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sasjs/core/main/base/mf_getattrc.sas

As opposed to: https://github.com/sasjs/core/blob/main/base/mf_getattrc.sas

If you click the links above you will see the difference. Whenever <sourcecode> begins with http:// or https:// we simply fetch the contents from the URL - so the raw value should be SAS code and nothing else.

You can find the raw version by clicking on the 'raw' button when viewing the program on github (next to the 'blame' button)

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Running some local SAS code: 

# create minimal SAS program
cat > ./somecode.sas <<'EOL'
  %put hello from SASjs;
EOL

# run the SAS code on the target
sasjs run somecode.sas -t myTarget

Running some SAS code from github:

sasjs run https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sasjs/template_jobs/master/includes/someprogram.sas -t viya

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text:
We plan to support the following:

  • keeping sessions alive
  • extracting items from the session

If there are items you are looking for, or have problems / ideas, do raise an issue.

docs.title: Runner
docs.text: SAS 9 has no API for running arbitrary code, so the CLI submits it to a stored process in your own metadata folder - the SASjs Runner. Deploy the runner once per user, and every SAS 9 operation works from then on.

docs.title: Which commands need it
docs.text:
On a SAS 9 target, every command that submits code goes through the runner:

  • sasjs run - the program you pass it
  • sasjs test - the test suite
  • sasjs fs - the synchronisation programs it generates
  • sasjs deploy - the deployScripts in the target's deployConfig

Commands that call a job or a web service directly - sasjs job, sasjs request - do not use it.

SAS Viya and SASjs Server need no runner.

docs.title: Where it lives
docs.text:
/User Folders/<your metadata user>/My Folder/sasjs/runner

The path follows the account the CLI authenticates as, so each SAS 9 user deploys their own. Nothing is shared and nothing needs an administrator.

docs.title: Deploying it
docs.text:
Run this once, in any SAS 9 session authenticated as that same user - Enterprise Guide, SAS Studio, or a stored process:

/* import the macros */
filename mc url "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sasjs/core/main/all.sas";
%inc mc;

/* create the runner */
filename ft15f001 temp;
parmcards4;
%macro sasjs_runner();
%if %symexist(_webin_fileref) %then %do;
%inc &_webin_fileref;
%end;
%mend sasjs_runner;
%sasjs_runner()
;;;;
%mm_createwebservice(
  path=/User Folders/&_metauser/My Folder/sasjs,
  name=runner
)

%mm_createwebservice creates the folder if it does not exist, registers the stored process, and makes it available as a SAS web service - which is what the CLI calls.

If your metadata user differs from the account you are signed in as, use the metadata user in the path= and name= arguments rather than &_metauser.

docs.title: When it is missing
docs.text:
The request comes back as a 404, and the CLI says so and prints the code above:

The SASjs runner was not found in your user folder at /User Folders/&_metauser/My Folder/sasjs/runner.
Please deploy the SASjs runner by running the code below and try again:

Deploying the runner and re-running the command is the whole fix. If the runner exists and the command still fails, the credentials are the next thing to check - sasjs auth for the target.

docs.title: SASjs Configuration
docs.text: The config file says what a project contains - where its jobs, services, macros and programs are - and where they deploy. Every command starts here.

docs.title: Where the file lives
docs.text:
File Scope Used when sasjs/sasjsconfig.json Project Any command run inside the project. The CLI walks up from the current folder and uses the nearest folder that holds a sasjs/sasjsconfig.json. ~/.sasjsrc User sasjs add with the global scope, and any command run outside a project.

A named target is looked up in the project file first and then in .sasjsrc, so a project can keep its own targets while the user file holds the rest. Where both files carry a target with the same name, the project one wins. Where no target is named, defaultTarget decides.

docs.title: Root level and target level
docs.text:
A setting belongs either at the root of the file, where it applies to every target, or inside a target, where it applies to that one. Three rules cover every key:

  • a scalar setting inside a target replaces the root-level value
  • folder arrays are combined - root folders first, then target folders, with duplicates removed - so a target adds folders rather than replacing them
  • a macro, program or binary file found in an earlier folder is the one used

docs.title: What the file holds
docs.text: Key Level Contents defaultTarget root the target used when a command runs without --target targets root the targets themselves, described below macroFolders root and target folders searched for SAS macros programFolders root and target folders searched for SAS Includes binaryFolders root and target folders searched for files embedded as base64 serviceConfig root and target serviceFolders, initProgram, termProgram, macroVars for services jobConfig root and target the same for jobs, with jobFolders testConfig root and target initProgram, termProgram, macroVars, testSetUp and testTearDown buildConfig root and target initProgram, termProgram, buildOutputFileName, macroVars for sasjs build deployConfig root and target deployScripts and deployServicePack for sasjs deploy docConfig root and target outDirectory, enableLineage, doxyContent, displayMacroCore, dataControllerUrl for sasjs doc streamConfig root and target the streaming app: webSourcePath, streamWebFolder, streamServiceName, streamWeb, streamLogo, assetPaths, and mockWeb / mockWebFolder - see sasjs web syncFolder root and target a folder copied as it is into the build output syncDirectories root and target local/remote pairs for sasjs fs sync sasjsBuildFolder, sasjsResultsFolder root and target where the build and the results go - sasjsbuild and sasjsresults by default httpsAgentOptions root and target TLS settings for the requests the CLI makes, such as caPath for an intermediate certificate

docs.title: A target
docs.text:
Key Meaning name how the target is addressed with --target serverType SASVIYA, SAS9 or SASJS serverUrl protocol, host and port of the SAS environment appLoc the SAS folder the project deploys into contextName the Viya compute context, eg SAS Job Execution compute context serverName, repositoryName SAS 9 only - where the SAS web services are deployed authConfig, authConfigSas9 credentials, saved here for a global target only httpsAgentOptions TLS settings for this target

Credentials for a local target are not in this file: they live in .env.<target> in the project, written by sasjs add - see the ENV file.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
Every key, with its type, defaults and allowed values, is generated from the JSON schema: sasjsconfig reference.

Adding $schema at the top of the file lets an editor that understands JSON schemas complete and check the keys as you type - this is what sasjs create and sasjs init write:

{
  "$schema": "https://cli.sasjs.io/sasjsconfig-schema.json",
  "defaultTarget": "viya",
  "targets": [
    {
      "name": "viya",
      "serverType": "SASVIYA",
      "serverUrl": "https://sas.example.com",
      "appLoc": "/Public/app"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: sasjs servicepack
docs.text: The sasjs servicepack command allows administrators to deploy the backend services for a SASjs app using a CI/CD framework of choice. Currently only the deploy action is supported, in future the export and create options will be made available. If you are waiting on these, please raise a github issue.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Before using this command, you will need to install the SASJS CLI and add a deployment target.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
sasjs servicepack <action> [additional arguments]

Additional arguments may include:

Option Alias Description --source -s The JSON file holding the services and folders to deploy. Required. --force -f Deploy even where folders and services already exist, overwriting them. --target -t The target to deploy to. Defaults to defaultTarget in sasjsconfig.json, then the global .sasjsrc.

Note

sasjs servicepack deploys to SAS Viya targets only; on any other server type the command stops with an error.

docs.title: Service Pack Structure
docs.text:
The service pack structure is designed to provide the bare minimum for defining remote services. It is normally created as part of the sasjs build comand when the target serverType is VIYA. For info, it looks like this:

{
 "members": [
  {
   "name": "services",
   "type": "folder",
   "members": [
    {
     "name": "admin",
     "type": "folder",
     "members": [
      {
       "name": "exportconfig",
       "type": "service",
       "code": "%put hello world;"
      }]
    }]
  }]
}

docs.title: sasjs servicepack deploy
docs.text: Used to deploy a servicepack to a Target. Note that the servicepack will be deployed to the appLoc defined in that target.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: sasjs servicepack deploy -s source.json -t target

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
# create minimal service pack
cat > ./servicepack.json <<'EOL'
{
 "members": [
  {
   "name": "services",
   "type": "folder",
   "members": [
    {
     "name": "public",
     "type": "folder",
     "members": [
      {
       "name": "hello",
       "type": "service",
       "code": "data _null_; file _webout; put 'Hello from SASjs';run;"
      }]
    }]
  }]
}
EOL

# deploy the service pack to the appLoc / server defined in the target (sasjs add)
sasjs servicepack deploy -s ./servicepack.json -t myTarget

docs.title: sasjs snippets
docs.text:
The sasjs snippets command generates VS Code snippets from any SAS macros contained in the folders (or subfolders) listed in the macroFolders array of the sasjs/sasjsconfig.json file. If macroFolders is defined at both configuration and target level, the two arrays will be merged in a single array of macro folders. Macros are those that fit the "$(macroname).sas" pattern - tests (such as macroname.test.sas or macroname.test.1.sas) are excluded, as are files with a non ".sas" extension.

Note - snippets are generated from the filename and doxygen header content, not the SAS code itself.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
sasjs snippets [options]
Option Alias Description --outDirectory -o Where to write the snippets file. Defaults to sasjsresults/sasjs-macro-snippets.json. --target -t The target whose macroFolders are read. Defaults to defaultTarget in sasjsconfig.json.

The macros come from the folders in macroFolders, and each snippet is built from the macro's Doxygen header - see the header conventions.

docs.title: Generate Snippets File
docs.text:
Consider the file name my/macros/example.sas:

/**
  @file
  @brief An example macro
  @details prints an arbitrary message to the log

  @param msg The message to be printed
  @author Allan Bowe

**/

%macro example(msg);

  %let testvar=%sysfunc(ranuni(0));

  data work.example;
    msg=symget('msg');
    putlog msg=;
  run;

%mend example ;

Assuming a sasjs/sasjsconfig.json file as follows:

{
  "$schema": "https://cli.sasjs.io/sasjsconfig-schema.json",
  "macroFolders": [
    "my/macros"
  ]
}

Simply run the sasjs snippets command within the SASjs project, and the following file will be written to sasjsresults/sasjs-macro-snippets.json:

{
  "example": {
    "prefix": "%example",
    "body": "%example($1)",
    "description": [
      "An example macro",
      "\r",
      "Params:\r",
      "-msg The message to be printed\r"
    ]
  }
}

Notice that the doxygen @brief value has been placed at the beginning of the description, and @param has been put to the Params section. The file name has been used to populate the prefix and body of the VS Code snippet, and placeholders are also created in the body.

docs.title: Import Snippets to VS Code
docs.text:
In order to import the generated VS Code snippets file please follow these steps:

  1. Open Command Pallet by pressing F1 (unix) or ctrl+shift+P (windows).
  2. Type Snippets: Configure User Snippets.
  3. Choose sas.json.
  4. Copy everything from the file generated by sasjs snippets command and paste it into sas.json.
  5. Save sas.json
  6. Snippets should be available in any .sas file by typing %<name of the snippet> (%example for the snippet from an example provided above).

docs.title: sasjs test
docs.text:
The sasjs test command triggers deployed SAS unit tests for execution, and collects the test results in JSON, JUnit XML, LCOV and CSV formats.

Results are also displayed in the console, as follows:

Tests are compiled & deployed as services (STPs in SAS 9, Jobs in Viya, Stored Programs in SASjs/server). In this way, every test is completely isolated with it's own SAS session.

To create a test, simply create a file with the same name as the Job / Service / Macro being tested, but with a .test.sas extension. If you have multiple tests, you can add a .test.[integer].sas extension, and the tests will proceed according to the integers provided.

You can send back one or more test results in a single program by creating a table called work.test_results with the following entries:

TEST_DESCRIPTION:$256 TEST_RESULT:$4 TEST_COMMENTS:$256 Some description PASS Some run related comment Another test description FAIL some explanation of the failure

The results should be sent back using the following macros (which could be in your termProgram entry):

/* do some tests */
data some sas tests;
  set whatever you like;
run;

/* create a test_results table */
data work.test_results;
  /* mandatory values */
  test_description="some description";
  test_result="PASS"; /* or FAIL */
  /* optional value */
  test_comments="We did this & that happened";
  output;
run;

/* send it back with the precompiled webout macro */
%webout(OPEN)
%webout(OBJ, TEST_RESULTS)
%webout(CLOSE)

Examples of tests for SAS Macros are available in the SASjs/CORE library. There are also a series of assertion macros available.

docs.title: Test Locations
docs.text:
Tests will only be compiled if they exist in a folder listed in one of the following sasjsconfig arrays:

  • macroFolders
  • jobFolders
  • serviceFolders

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
sasjs test [filteringString..] [options]
Option Alias Description --source -s The test flow to execute. Defaults to sasjsbuild/testFlow.json, which sasjs build writes. --outDirectory --out Folder for the results. Defaults to sasjsresults. --force -f Run every test even when some fail, and exit 0 - for a pipeline that reports rather than gates. --target -t The target to run the tests against. Defaults to defaultTarget in sasjsconfig.json.

Each filteringString is a regular expression, matched against the test paths in the flow; only the tests that match are run. With none, every test in the flow runs. The set-up and tear-down programs always run.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Execute all tests for the default target:

sasjs test

Execute all tests in the macros folder:

sasjs test /macros/

Execute all tests starting with "mv_" and save the output in 'myresults' folder

sasjs test mv_ --outDirectory /somedir/myresults

Prevent the command failing (for example in a CI pipeline that reports rather than gates):

sasjs test --force

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Test configuration can be provided at root or target level. Configuration example:

"testConfig": {
  "initProgram": "sasjs/tests/testinit.sas",
  "termProgram": "sasjs/tests/testterm.sas",
  "macroVars": {
    "testVar": "testValue"
  },
  "testSetUp": "sasjs/tests/testsetup.sas",
  "testTearDown": "sasjs/tests/testteardown.sas"
}
  • testSetUp will be executed prior to all tests
  • testTearDown will be executed after all tests have finished
  • initProgram is inserted at the start of every test
  • termProgram is inserted at the end of every test
  • macroVars are defined at the start of every test

docs.title: File Name Convention
docs.text:
Only files names that match following pattern will be considered as tests. Pattern:

[filename].test<.integer>.sas

Examples:

some_service.test.sas
some_job.test.0.sas
some_job.test.1.sas
  • Providing a test integer is optional, if provided, the tests will be executed accordingly to numerical order - eg some_job.test.0.sas first and some_job.test.1.sas second.

docs.title: Coverage
docs.text:
A SAS Service, Job or Macro is considered covered if there is a test file with the same filename, for example:

├── some_service.sas
├── some_service.test.sas
├── some_job.sas
└── some_macro.test.sas

In the example above, some_service will be considered covered, some_job will be considered not covered and some_macro.test will be considered as a standalone test.

Overall coverage is displayed, along with a group summary for Jobs, Services and Macros. The table lists every service, job and macro the compile found, marked as covered or not covered, followed by any standalone tests - the same rows and the same keys that sasjs compile writes to sasjsbuild/coverage.json.

Note

We are planning a more 'intelligent' coverage system that can detect whether a macro / servivce / job was executed as part of the test suite. If this would be helpful to your project, do get in touch!

docs.title: Test Body
docs.text:
An example of a test that provides a result:

data work.test_results;
  test_description="some description";
  test_result="PASS";
  test_comments="We did this & that happened";
  output;
run;
%webout(OPEN)
%webout(OBJ, test_results)
%webout(CLOSE)

Providing the test_results table with a test_result variable is required, in order for the frontend to determine if the test is a PASS or FAIL. The webout() macro definition will be deployed as precode in the compiled test, and is essentially a wrapper for mm_webout.sas or mv_webout.sas according the serverType of the target.

docs.title: Test Flow
docs.text: SAS unit tests will be executed one after another. Execution order is described in sasjsbuild/testFlow.json which is created as part of compilation process (sasjs compile).

docs.title: Test Results
docs.text:
By default test results will be saved in the sasjsresults folder. An example of sasjsresults folder structure:

├── logs
│  ├── macros_some_macro.test.1.log
│  ├── macros_some_macro.test.log
│  ├── services_some_service.test.log
│  ├── jobs_some_job.test.log
│  ├── testteardown.log
│  └── testsetup.log
├── testResults.csv
└── testResults.json
└── testResults.xml

Results are saved in CSV, JSON and JUnit XML formats.

docs.title: Assertion Macros
docs.text:
A number of ready made assertion macros are available in the SASjs Core library:

  • mp_assert - generic assertion
  • mp_assertcols - Asserts the existence (or not) of certain columns
  • mp_assertcolvals - Asserts the existence (or not) of particular column values
  • mp_assertdsobs - Asserts the existence (or not) of dataset observations
  • mp_assertscope - Compares before/after to detect scope leakage in a SAS Macro

docs.title: Running SAS Tests with SASjs
docs.text:
In order to run tests, take the following steps:

  1. Provide tests configuration (testConfig) in the sasjs/sasjsconfig.json file
  2. Create test files in services, jobs or macro folders (with .test.sas extension).
  3. Execute sasjs cbd -t <targetName> to compile and deploy the tests as isolated SAS web services
  4. Execute sasjs test -t <targetName>
  5. Visit the local sasjsresults folder to review results.

To assist with debugging, all logs are captured, and we generate a URL so that you can easily click and re-run any particular individual test.

docs.title: sasjs version
docs.text: sasjs version prints the version of the SASjs CLI you are running.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
sasjs version
sasjs v
sasjs -v
sasjs --version

All four are the same command. It takes no arguments and needs no target or project.

Example:

$ sasjs --version
You are using SASjs CLI v6.4.7

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The version is read from the package that is running, so it is right whichever way the CLI was installed - globally, into a project, through npx, or from a temporary prefix.
  • A CLI running from a source checkout (npm link, or a local build) reports itself as a linked version, with the path it runs from. A source checkout carries no version of its own until it is packaged, so no version number is shown.
  • -v and --version are accepted from 6.4.7. Earlier releases reject them, and report a version only when the CLI is installed globally.

To see the commands available in the installed version, use sasjs help.

docs.title: sasjs web
docs.text:
sasjs web builds the streaming web app services - the frontend, packaged so that it can be served from the SAS folder tree instead of the SAS Web Server.

It does the web part of compilation on its own: the same work sasjs compile does when streamConfig.streamWeb is true, without compiling the jobs and services.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
sasjs web [options]

sasjs w is the alias.

Option Alias Description --target -t The target whose streamConfig drives the build. Defaults to the defaultTarget in sasjsconfig.json.

Example:

sasjs web -t myTarget

docs.title: What it needs
docs.text:
The project, or the target, must configure streamConfig - the target's values win where both set a key:

"streamConfig": {
  "streamWeb": true,
  "webSourcePath": "../client/dist",
  "streamWebFolder": "webv",
  "streamServiceName": "clickme"
}
  • webSourcePath must be a folder that exists, relative to the project root, and it must contain an index.html
  • streamWebFolder is the folder below the target's appLoc that receives the services
  • streamServiceName names the service that serves index.html - clickme by default

webSourcePath and streamWebFolder are both required, and the folder and its index.html are checked: the command stops with a message naming whichever is missing.

docs.title: What it produces
docs.text:
Server type Output SAS Viya A service per linked asset, plus the clickme service for index.html, written below sasjsbuild/services/<streamWebFolder> SAS 9 The same services, created for the SAS 9 web service model SASjs Server The contents of webSourcePath, copied to the same folder - SASjs Server serves the files directly, so no services are generated

Tags in index.html are rewritten to point at the generated services, replacing the references to the original asset files.

The services land in the build folder, so they are deployed by the next sasjs build and sasjs deploy - or by sasjs cbd.
